plugin_name: Command Injection with Verbose Scanner Output
description: Command injection identified in the CI pipeline build trigger API. The build_command parameter is passed directly to a shell without sanitisation. An attacker with access to the CI API can execute arbitrary operating system commands with the privileges of the CI service account. The affected endpoint is POST /api/ci/trigger and the vulnerable parameter is build_command. Exploitation requires a valid API token, which may be obtained via credential stuffing, phishing, or previous vulnerability chaining. Once code execution is achieved, an attacker can pivot to connected internal systems, exfiltrate source code, inject malicious code into build artefacts, or tamper with deployment pipelines. The CI service runs as a low-privilege user; however, access to the service account's SSH keys and cloud provider credentials stored in environment variables enables lateral movement. Historical incidents involving similar vulnerabilities in CI/CD platforms (e.g. CircleCI 2022 breach, Codecov 2021 supply-chain attack) demonstrate that CI compromise has extremely high business impact. Remediation requires immediate patching of the affected build trigger endpoint, rotation of all secrets accessible to the CI service, audit of recent build logs for signs of compromise, and implementation of strict input validation using an allowlist of permitted characters for build command parameters. Additional hardening steps include least-privilege service accounts, network egress filtering to prevent data exfiltration, signed build artefacts, and mandatory two-person review for changes to CI configuration files. The engineering team should also evaluate whether the build_command parameter is necessary or whether it can be replaced by a reference to a predefined build configuration identifier, which would eliminate the injection surface entirely.
solution: Validate build_command against a strict allowlist. Rotate all CI secrets. Audit recent build logs.
plugin_output: Injected ; id > /tmp/pwned into build_command. CI response included uid=1001(ci-runner) in log output.
